_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's featured sponsor template (studio/templates.py make --spec). Its film is projects/featured-sponsor (local: the sponsor's and the event's logos and the event's key art are third-party). The sample: Red Hat, a Diamond sponsor of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 (Salt Lake City, Nov 9-12; events.linuxfoundation.org/kubecon-cloudnativecon-north-america). v3 (2026-10-05) is a film written by hand in the event's own look, after the owner called the minted-coin film (v1, v2; kitcut.ai film studio-20261005-122631-gzityz) cringe and off both style books: no coin, no press, no metal; the event's ground, type, buttons and key art, and the sponsor's logo flat on a solid panel with clear space. It is not a pull of that studio film any more, so `prove` does not apply.
title: Featured sponsor
description: A 26-second thank-you to one sponsor of one event, with no narration, every beat on the music, in the event's own look. The event's ground colour fills the frame, its key art drifts along the bottom and its logo sits top right, as on its own social card; 'THANK YOU TO OUR' arrives small and tracked, then the tier, large: 'DIAMOND SPONSOR'. On the music's hit the art drops away, a line opens into a white panel with rounded corners and the sponsor's logo is there: flat, whole, still, with clear space on every side. The panel settles into one block with the words, balanced in the space above the art: the tier over a thin rule, one line about the sponsor in their own words set as large as the frame allows, and where to find them as a button in the event's colour (the panel above the words in a square or vertical frame, a tall panel beside them in a wide one). The panel then grows into a sponsor wall like the event's own sponsor page: a white ground, the tier in light tracked capitals over its rule, the logo large. The wall drops away to the sign-off: the dates and the city in bold capitals over the art in full colour, the venue, and the link as a button.
author: KitCut
example: Welcome Northwind as a Gold sponsor of our conference, PlatformCon 2027, June 3-4 in Berlin. Find them at booth B12 for live demos. Their logo and ours are attached.
brief:
The film thanks ONE sponsor of ONE event the way the event's own designer would post it: flat, typographic, in the EVENT's look, with the sponsor's logo treated by the sponsor's rules. Keep the five beats, the clock and the sound; change the content. There is no coin, no medal, no 3D and no effect anywhere: do not add one.

READ THE TWO STYLE BOOKS FIRST. The event: open its site and its own social card or banner, and take from them its ground colour, its two button colours, its type (fetch its own font files when the site serves them) and its key art. The sponsor: open its brand or logo page when it publishes one and follow it (clear space, which logo goes on which ground). Never a costume taken from the event's name, never a colour neither of them uses.

THE SPONSOR'S LOGO is drawn exactly as its file draws it, flat and whole, on a solid panel with clear space of at least a quarter of its height on every side (the code keeps more). The film fades it in and moves it with its panel; it never turns, tilts, stretches, recolours, shades, outlines or lights a logo, never crops one inside the frame, and never lays one on the art or on a gradient. Say its ink honestly: logo.ink 'dark' (dark ink: the panel is white) or 'light' (a white logo: the panel is sponsor.color, their own dark or brand colour). Use the version their rules give for that ground. logo.clear: more clear space, as a part of the logo's height, when their rules ask for it. logo.named: false when the logo is a symbol that does not spell the name (the name is then set in type beside it). With no logo file the name stands on the panel in type: never a drawn or guessed logo.

content.json (SK.DATA.content): sponsor {name; logo {image: a picture key, ink, clear, named}; line: ONE line about who they are, in their own words from their site, at most ~60 characters so it sets large (up to three lines; a longer one is set smaller and cut with an ellipsis, so shorten it at a clause, never rewrite it), or ""; tier: the tier in the event's own word, upper case ('GOLD'), only if the event's page or the person says it, else "" (the film then says copy.featured); find: where to find them (a booth, a session, an offer; at most ~32 characters), only if published or given, else ""; link: their shortest address without https://, or ""; color: their brand colour (the panel's colour under a white logo)}. event {name, year, dates ('NOVEMBER 9-12, 2026'), city, venue or "", tags: its own hashtags or "", url: the shortest address that opens the event, without https:// (an address too long to read is cut back to its site by the code), logo {image, ink: 'light' for a white logo on the ground, 'dark' for a dark one, which then gets a white plate}, art {image, top, bright, bright_top}}. copy {thanks ('THANK YOU TO OUR', or ""), tier ('{tier} SPONSOR': the large line and the button), featured ('FEATURED SPONSOR': the line when there is no tier), wall ('{tier}': the heading on the sponsor wall), more (a last small line such as 'MORE SPONSORS SOON', usually ""), arrow}: copy lines may name a field in braces ({tier}, {year}, {sponsor}); translate them for another language. palette {ground: the event's ground colour, accent and second: its two button colours, light, dark}. fonts {head, body, weights {bold, mid, light}} only when the event's own faces were fetched (name the weights that exist).

THE KEY ART (event.art) is the event's OWN published picture: its banner, its social card's illustration, a photo it posts. Fetch it with the picture tool from its site; crop off any text, logo or date baked into it (the film sets those in type); never generate, redraw, recolour or animate pieces of it. `bright` is the picture in full colour, for the opening and the sign-off; `image` is the quiet version the site runs behind a page (when it has one), for the scenes where the sponsor is on; either serves for both. `top` and `bright_top` (0 to 0.7) leave out a picture's empty upper part. With no art at all the ground stays flat and the layout closes over it: that is better than a picture that is not theirs.

Limits, all fitted by the code: the tier line up to three lines; the sponsor's line up to three; a name in type up to two; long venues and hashtags wrap to two lines; a long event name with no logo file wraps as a masthead. A fact that is missing is left out and the layout closes over it: no tier, no line, no booth, no link, no venue, no hashtags, no art. With nothing to say beside the logo, the panel simply holds its place until the wall.

Pictures become the film's own with template_pictures: logo= the event's logo; logos=[...] the sponsor's logo. An attached picture first, else the one on the sponsor's or the event's own site (a brand or press page). Name each picture's key in content.json.

NEVER INVENT. Every fact is the person's own, from their words, their attachments or the event's and the sponsor's own pages on the web: no made-up tier, booth number, session, offer or description. When the tier the person names differs from the event's sponsor page, keep theirs and say so in the reply. A fact that cannot be found is left out.

The frame is the person's choice: square and vertical set the panel above the words; wide sets it beside them. Check the stills of the reveal (about 6 s), who they are (13 s), the wall (17.5 s) and the sign-off (23 s) after changing the content: the logo whole with space round it, every word readable on a phone, nothing over the art.
